# Managed data layout

`HSUM_HOME` places all managed state below one absolute root. The paths below are produced by the same resolver used at runtime.

Generated from hSUM `0.1.0-alpha.4`.

```text
/HSUM_HOME
├── config
│   ├── config.toml
│   ├── trusted-projects.toml
│   └── integration-policy.toml
├── data
│   ├── managed-backups.json
│   └── indexes
│       └── index-name
│           └── index.sqlite
└── cache
    └── models
```

| Purpose | Resolved path |
|---|---|
| User configuration | `/HSUM_HOME/config/config.toml` |
| Trust registry | `/HSUM_HOME/config/trusted-projects.toml` |
| Integration policy | `/HSUM_HOME/config/integration-policy.toml` |
| Managed backup registry | `/HSUM_HOME/data/managed-backups.json` |
| Index database | `/HSUM_HOME/data/indexes/index-name/index.sqlite` |
| Model cache | `/HSUM_HOME/cache/models` |


The repository-side `.hsum.toml` pointer is optional and is not stored below `HSUM_HOME`. It is only a selection hint: authorization remains in the private trust registry. SQLite sidecars, maintenance staging, quarantine, and backup files are implementation-managed and must not be edited by hand. Use `hsum context`, `hsum backup`, and the plan/apply maintenance commands instead.
